topics: 🚪 Deference at Doorways — Ravin, Abaye, and Rabbi Yoḥanan's rule about doorways worthy of a mezuza
🍞 Table Manners — waiting for the one who breaks bread, sharing a dish, and saying it in the teacher's words
🙏 Answering Amen — the abbreviated, truncated, and orphaned amen; Rav Ḥisda's 'majority' rule
🍄 Joining Late — Rav, Shmuel, and the truffles; who recites the blessing for the group
🌾 Demai, Tithes, and Redemption — why the mishna teaches cases that seem obvious
👥 Who Counts for Ten — Kutim, the am ha'aretz, a convert not yet immersed, a slave, and 'nine that look like ten'

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Honor at the Table and the Boundaries of a Zimmun
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 47a–47b
overview.hebrewSource: אֵין מְכַבְּדִין אֶלָּא בְּפֶתַח שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ מְזוּזָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens with stories about honor: Ravin only defers to Abaye at the synagogue door, diners wait for the one who breaks bread, and the one who breaks bread waits for the amen to finish. The Gemara then defines a proper amen and warns against the hasty or 'orphaned' amen. Returning to zimmun, it explains why the mishna bothered to list obviously permitted and forbidden foods (demai, first tithe, redeemed second tithe), why a Kuti is counted but an am ha'aretz is not, and how a group completes a quorum of ten — with a minor, a slave, or even two scholars who sharpen each other in halakha.

slides.title: 🚪 Ravin and Abaye on the Road: Where Does One Defer?
slides.subtitle: A small slight on a donkey ride leads to a rule about doorways

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: Ravin's donkey went ahead of mine and he did not say 'Let the Master go first'. Ever since he came up from the West he has become arrogant!

lines.speaker: Ravin
lines.text: At the synagogue door: Let the Master enter first.

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: Until now was I not Master? Why defer to me only here and not on the road?

lines.speaker: Ravin
lines.text: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: אֵין מְכַבְּדִין אֶלָּא בְּפֶתַח שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ מְזוּזָה — one defers only at a doorway that has a mezuza.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Only where there is a mezuza? Then at a synagogue or study hall, which have no mezuza, would one not defer?

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: Say rather: at a doorway worthy of a mezuza — but not on a road or a bridge.

callout.label: Say it in your teacher's words:
callout.text: Rav said diners may not eat until the one who breaks bread has tasted. Rav Safra insisted the word was 'taste', not 'eat'. There is no practical difference — the lesson is that one must repeat a teaching in the exact language of one's teacher.

slides.title: 🍞 Rules of the Table and the Proper Amen
slides.subtitle: Small courtesies that the Sages turned into halakha
rows: Diners wait for the one who breaks bread to taste
Rav (via Rav Yehuda b. Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat)
No one at the table may taste anything before him
Two eating from one dish wait for each other
Baraita
Three need not wait; everyone eats when he wishes
The one who breaks bread reaches out first
Baraita
But he may defer to his teacher or to someone greater than he
Do not break the bread until the amen has ended
Rabba bar bar Ḥana, teaching his son
Rav Ḥisda: until the amen of the majority has ended — one who drags out his amen is simply mistaken
No amen ḥatufa, ketufa, or yetoma
Baraita
Not with the first syllable swallowed, not with the second cut off, not without knowing which blessing you answer
Do not toss a blessing from your mouth
Baraita
A blessing should not be discharged quickly and indifferently
Measure for measure
Ben Azzai
An orphaned amen — his children orphaned; an abbreviated amen — his days abbreviated; one who extends his amen — his days and years are extended

callout.label: Joining late:
callout.text: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya arrived late and ate hurriedly to join Rav and Shmuel's zimmun. Rav said: we have finished. Shmuel replied: if they brought me truffles, or a young pigeon for Abba, wouldn't we still eat? The meal is not over. When Rav Aḥa arrived at the students' meal he claimed a main participant should recite, but the halakha is that the greatest person recites, even if he came at the end.

slides.title: 🌾 Why Does the Mishna Teach the Obvious?
slides.subtitle: Each 'peshita' hides a borderline case

nodes.content: ❓ The mishna lists foods whose eaters join a zimmun — but each case seems obvious. What is it really teaching?

columns.label: Demai
columns.content: Forbidden to him? He could declare his property ownerless, become poor, and the poor may eat demai (though Beit Shammai disagree, per Rav Huna).

columns.label: First tithe, teruma taken
columns.content: The Levite took it while the grain was still on the stalks and separated only teruma of the tithe. Reish Lakish: 'a tenth of the tithe' (Num. 18:26) — no teruma gedola needed.

columns.label: Redeemed second tithe / hekdesh
columns.content: He paid the principal but not the added fifth. Lesson: the missing fifth does not invalidate the redemption. Likewise a waiter who ate an olive-bulk counts as a participant.

nodes.content: 🔁 Rav Pappa to Abaye: then even a Levite who took his tithe from the pile should be exempt! Abaye: 'From all your tithes you shall set apart' (Num. 18:29) — once threshed and piled it is 'grain', and the priest's share applies.

columns.label: Tevel
columns.content: Only rabbinic tevel: grown in an unperforated flowerpot.

columns.label: Improperly redeemed
columns.content: Second tithe redeemed with an unminted coin — 'bind up the money' (Deut. 14:25) means stamped coin; hekdesh exchanged for land, not money (Lev. 27:19).

columns.label: Gentile
columns.content: A convert who was circumcised but has not immersed — Rabbi Yoḥanan: until he immerses he is a gentile.

callout.label: Method:
callout.text: Whenever the Gemara says 'peshita' (obvious), the answer is a narrower case the mishna must have had in mind.

slides.title: 🧑‍🌾 Who Is an Am Ha'aretz — and Why a Kuti Still Counts
slides.subtitle: The mishna counts a Kuti; a baraita excludes an am ha'aretz

boxes.title: Defining the am ha'aretz (tithes and purity)
items: Rabbi Meir: one who does not eat ordinary food in ritual purity
The Rabbis: one who does not tithe his produce properly
Rava: the exclusion follows the Rabbis — and Kutim tithe scrupulously, being exacting in any mitzva they embraced, even more than Jews
Abaye's alternative: the mishna speaks of a Kuti who is a ḥaver

boxes.title: Defining the am ha'aretz (the baraita)
items: Rabbi Eliezer: does not recite Shema evening and morning
Rabbi Yehoshua: does not don tefillin
Ben Azzai: no tzitzit on his garment
Rabbi Natan: no mezuza on his door
Rabbi Natan bar Yosef: has children but does not raise them to Torah study
Aḥerim: even one who read Bible and studied Mishna but did not serve Torah scholars — Rav Huna: the halakha follows Aḥerim

boxes.title: A cautionary tale
items: Rami bar Ḥama refused to include Rav Menashya bar Taḥlifa, who had studied Sifra, Sifrei, and halakhot, in a zimmun
Rava: Rami bar Ḥama died only because of that
Answer 1: Rav Menashya did serve the Sages; Rami bar Ḥama simply failed to check
Answer 2: one who hears halakhot from the Sages and reviews them is like a Torah scholar

callout.label: Takeaway:
callout.text: Exclusion from a zimmun is serious; a person's Torah standing must be examined carefully before he is left out.

slides.title: 🔟 Completing a Quorum of Ten
slides.subtitle: Who — or what — may serve as the tenth?

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rabbi Yosei: a minor in a cradle is counted. The Gemara reconciles this with the mishna via Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: he is not counted for a zimmun of three, but may be an adjunct to complete ten
2️⃣ Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: nine and a slave join. Objection: Rabbi Eliezer freed his slave to complete a minyan! Answer: two were missing — he freed one and used the other unfreed
3️⃣ But Rav Yehuda says freeing a Canaanite slave violates 'they shall serve you forever' (Lev. 25:46)! Answer: a mitzva that benefits the many is different
4️⃣ Rav Huna: nine and the ark join. Rav Naḥman: is an ark a man? Rather — nine that appear like ten, whether gathered or scattered

5️⃣ Rav Ami: two and Shabbat join. Rav Naḥman: is Shabbat a man? Rather — two scholars who sharpen each other in halakha count as three. Rav Ḥisda: like me and Rav Sheshet; Rav Sheshet: like me and Rav Ḥisda
6️⃣ Rabbi Yoḥanan: a mature minor who shows signs of puberty is counted; a baraita adds that one is not exacting about a minor
7️⃣ Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: rise early to be among the first ten in the synagogue — even if a hundred come after, you receive a reward equivalent to them all

callout.label: Note:
callout.text: The Gemara emends 'receives the reward of them all' to 'a reward equivalent to them all' — no one takes away another's reward.

summary.principle: Honor at the table and in the synagogue has rules — where to defer, when to eat, how to answer amen — and a zimmun of ten is completed only by people who truly belong to it.

flowSteps.content: 🚪 Rabbi Yoḥanan: defer to a greater person only at a doorway worthy of a mezuza, not on the road
🍞 Wait for the one who breaks bread; he waits for the majority's amen; no ḥatufa, ketufa, or yetoma amen
❓ Why teach obvious cases? Demai (could become poor), first tithe on the stalks, redemption without the fifth, rabbinic tevel, asimon, convert not immersed

columns.content: 👥 A Kuti counts: he tithes properly, so he is no am ha'aretz by the Rabbis' definition
🔟 Completing ten: a minor as adjunct, a slave, nine that look like ten, two scholars who sharpen each other

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: The greatest person recites the blessing even if he arrived last — and rising early to be among the first ten earns a reward equal to all who follow

quiz.q: Why did Ravin defer to Abaye only when they reached the synagogue door?
o: Because the synagogue is holier than the road
Because Rabbi Yoḥanan taught that one defers only at a doorway worthy of a mezuza, not on a road or bridge
Because Abaye was the older of the two
Because Ravin had only just noticed Abaye
quiz.e: Ravin cited Rabbi Yoḥanan: one shows deference only at a doorway with a mezuza. The Gemara refines this to a doorway worthy of a mezuza, so that synagogues and study halls are included but roads and bridges are not.

quiz.q: Why does Rav Ḥisda hold that the one who breaks bread need only wait for the majority's amen to end?
o: Because the minority's amen does not count
Because a blessing is finished as soon as the leader stops speaking
Because anyone who prolongs his amen excessively is simply mistaken
Because only the majority is obligated to answer
quiz.e: Rami bar Ḥama asked why the minority's unfinished amen does not delay the breaking of bread. Rav Ḥisda answered that one who answers an amen of excessive length is mistaken, so there is no need to wait for him.

quiz.q: How can one who ate demai be counted in a zimmun, when demai is forbidden to him?
o: Demai is permitted to everyone after the fact
If he wished he could declare his property ownerless and become poor, and the poor may eat demai
The mishna follows Beit Shammai
Demai only requires tithing by rabbinic law, which is ignored for zimmun
quiz.e: Since he could make himself a pauper by declaring his property hefker, and the mishna permits feeding demai to the poor, the demai is considered fit for him.

quiz.q: According to Rava, why is a Kuti counted in a zimmun even though an am ha'aretz is not?
o: Because Kutim are considered full ḥaverim in all matters
Because the exclusion follows the Rabbis' definition of an am ha'aretz — one who does not tithe properly — and Kutim tithe scrupulously
Because the baraita excluding an am ha'aretz is not accepted as halakha
Because Rabbi Meir holds that eating in purity is not required
quiz.e: Rava explains that the baraita excluding an am ha'aretz follows the Rabbis, who define him as one who does not tithe properly. Kutim are exacting in any mitzva they accepted, including tithing, so they are not an am ha'aretz in this sense. Abaye instead says the mishna speaks of a Kuti who is a ḥaver.

quiz.q: Rav Huna said 'nine and the ark join'. How did the Gemara understand his final position?
o: An ark containing Torah scrolls may literally be counted as the tenth
Nine people together with any sacred object form a quorum
Nine who appear like ten — whether gathered or scattered — may join together
Nine people may recite the zimmun of ten if they intended to gather ten
quiz.e: Rav Naḥman objected, 'Is an ark a man?' Rav Huna then restated his view: nine that look like ten join together, and the Gemara records two versions of what creates that impression — when they are gathered, or when they are scattered.
